business.title: What kind of business is this?
business.description: e.g. 'a café with 12 staff', 'a small bike shop'.

tools.name: roster_status
tools.description: This week and next: the open spots (soonest first, with who is free for each), conflicts, everyone's hours against their limits, the schedule by day, availability and the business's rules, all with ids. Call it first when asked where you're short, who is working, or how many hours someone has. Pass week for another week.

week.description: Any date in the week, YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.name: add_staff
tools.description: Save a person on the roster: name, the roles they work, and their own weekly hour limit if the business states one. An existing name is updated, never duplicated; status inactive takes someone off the active staff. Call it as soon as a person is mentioned, before you describe it.

roles.description: What they work, comma-separated, e.g. 'barista, kitchen'.

maxHours.description: Their own weekly hour limit, only as the business states it.

tools.name: set_availability
tools.description: Record when someone can't work: a weekday for every week, weekdays, weekends, every day, or one date, all day or for part of it. available true clears it. Call it the moment the person tells you; it names any shift that now clashes.

day.description: A weekday ('tuesday') for every week, 'weekdays', 'weekends', 'every day', or a date (YYYY-MM-DD) for one day.

available.description: True when they can work that day again.

date.description: Only with day 'one date': the date, YYYY-MM-DD.

tools.name: add_shift
tools.description: Add a shift: date, start, end, role and how many people it needs. A shift with the same date, start and role is updated, never duplicated. Call it as soon as a shift is mentioned.

role.description: What the shift works, e.g. 'barista' or 'kitchen'.

tools.name: copy_week
tools.description: Start a week from another one (default: the week before), keeping each person only where they still pass every rule and availability. Existing shifts are never duplicated. Use it to draft next week in one call.

week.description: Any date in the week to fill.

fromWeek.description: Any date in the week to copy (default: the week before).

tools.name: assign_shift
tools.description: Put someone on a shift (staff) or take someone off (remove), by the shift's id. It refuses a person who is unavailable, already working, short of rest or over their hours, and names who is free instead. Your assignments are proposals: the person approves each week on the roster page.

id.description: The shift id from roster_status, e.g. 'sh-4'.

date.description: Without an id: the shift date, YYYY-MM-DD.

start.description: Without an id: the start time.

staff.description: Who to put on it: name or id.

remove.description: Who to take off it: name or id.

tools.name: set_rules
tools.description: Record a scheduling rule the business states: most hours a week, fewest hours between shifts, longest shift, or another rule in their words. Only ever record rules they state; never add your own.

maxWeekHours.description: Most hours a week per person (0 removes the rule).

minRestHours.description: Fewest hours between shifts (0 removes the rule).

maxShiftHours.description: Longest shift in hours (0 removes the rule).

rule.description: Any other rule, in the business's own words.

forget.description: Drop the written rule containing this text.

maxHours.description: Their own weekly hour limit, only as the business states it.

start.description: Without an id: the start time.

available.description: True when they can work that day again.

date.description: Only with day 'one date': the date, YYYY-MM-DD.
